title: GitHub connection
description: Sign in on GitHub with a one-time code. GitHub will identify the authorization helper as Git Credential Manager.
privacy: Credentials are protected by this computer’s credential store. They are not sent to Seigr or included in workspace copies or published websites.
permissions: Git Credential Manager requests repository, workflow and gist access. Your organization may require approval before its repositories are available.
disconnected: No GitHub account is connected to this workspace.
waiting: Finish signing in on GitHub using the code below. Waiting for authorization…
deviceInstructions: Open GitHub and enter this one-time code. Confirm the account and organization access you want to use.
deviceReturn: Return to Observanda after authorizing. This panel updates automatically; no localhost page is needed.
saving: Protecting your connection on this computer…
forgetHint: Forgetting removes Observanda’s saved credential and disconnects this account from all Observanda workspaces on this computer.
unavailable: Browser sign-in needs the bundled Git Credential Manager and Git runtime. Use a current Observanda installation.
tokenHint: For managed or headless installations, you can use a token with access to your repository. It stays in memory until disconnect or restart. Pages setup also needs Pages and Administration write permissions.
temporary: A temporary token is connected for this session.
connectToBrowse: Sign in with GitHub to choose an account, organization and repository.
organizationAccess: Organization not listed? Its GitHub administrators may need to approve Git Credential Manager or authorize single sign-on. Refresh this list after granting access.
noRepositories: No writable repositories on this page. Check the next page or the account?s repository permissions.
manualDestination: You can also enter the owner, repository and branch below. Choosing a destination updates these fields; save when ready.
requestingCode: Requesting a sign-in code from GitHub?
repositoryOwners: This connection lists organizations through repositories it can access. An organization may appear on more than one page. You can enter an owner below when creating a new repository.
